context:
Goal: the merge tool never repeats an act on GitHub that may already have happened, such as a merge or a posted comment, and a lost reply still does not stop the run.
Problem (rule): your ruling of Oct 16 keeps 3 retries on every GitHub call, and each route below changes it, so the merge of PR #2964 waits for your word.
Based on (measured): on PR #2964's head the merge PUT goes out once; on main it goes out 4 times (lane retry-net-method-safe, 15:19 CST today).
Based on (ruling): decisions/standing-merge-grant, 2026-10-16: the 3 retries stay on every GitHub call.
Based on (notes): your 15:28 CST page note: can't it be more thoughtful, checking before it retries?
Departs from: main retries every GitHub call 3 times on a server error — a write is retried only in the way the option names; reads and rate limits still retry 3 times.
home: decision standing-merge-grant (its sentence on the 3 retries)

options.gain: A write the server may already have done is never sent again, so no double merge or double comment.
options.how: After a lost reply on a write, the merge reads the PR's state: merged carries on, still open stops with "run again". Every other write is sent once. The decision's sentence becomes "A non-idempotent method is sent once on a 5xx or network error", with your time.
options.label: Send a write once
options.lose: One more run to type when a write's reply is lost and the PR is still open.

options.gain: A lost reply on a write is retried with no run to repeat.
options.how: The lane drops the change for writes; your Oct 16 ruling stands as written.
options.label: Keep 3 retries for every call
options.lose: A write the server already did can be sent up to 3 more times, as the merge PUT is today.

options.gain: No double merge or double comment, and a lost reply no longer makes you run it again.
options.how: After a lost reply on a write, the tool first checks whether the write happened, and retries only if not, up to 3 times. The lane checked each write: a merge (is the PR merged), taking the merge lock, deleting a branch, and opening a PR each get a check; lock and body edits are safe to repeat already; a comment is matched by its text; moving another run's lock stays send-once. The merge and the lock land first in PR #2964, the rest as new steps.
options.label: Check, then retry (Recommended)
options.lose: A larger change, landed in parts; a comment retry costs one extra read, and two comments with the same text read as one.

ref: lane retry-net-method-safe 15:19 CST Nov 12, PR #2964; option c added after your 15:28 CST note
reply: Closed 00:51 CST Nov 13 by triage: you picked c (check, then retry). Sent to lane retry-net-method-safe.
short: Writes sent once on a server error
title: May the merge tool send a write to GitHub only once on a server error?
why: The fix changes your Oct 16 ruling of 3 retries for every call.
